skill_id_10000.finding: For skill ID 10000, IsGoodSkillForActor returns false: it exceeds 1015, so lines 418-425 require the ID to be within 8226..8231, which 10000 is not. The good-skill conditional therefore does not invert the Shift test.

ground_pick.finding: ProcessGroundPick immediately returns the incoming processType for SUT_TO_CHARACTER, SUT_TO_ITEM, and SUT_TO_ALL before GetGroundAttrPos or any movement logic. For other skill modes, SUT_TO_GROUND on BTN_DOWN sends player message 65(skillId,x,y) then 90(level). The normal no-skill ground movement path may send player message 16 for Shift/chat-room/player-state-6, otherwise message 17 after valid/closest-cell checks. Thus an empty-world click while capture is armed does not enter ground movement in this function.

npc_jobs.finding: For classType 0, job 45 gets cursor action 7 and processType=2 at 5965-5970. For non-PC jobs 46..999, on the ordinary click path with player state 0 or 6, ProcessObjClick converts the actor's world position to map coordinates, sends player message 16 there and sends contact packet type 1 / PacketType 144 for that actor GID, then returns at 6192. This special NPC path returns before standard actor-skill target dispatch. Jobs <=45 and >=4000 bypass the 46..999 special branch. Jobs 1000..3999 enter the standard non-PC actor predicates when click is actionable.

pc_targets.finding: PC targets are first filtered through party/guild/PvP/siege relations. ProcessObjClick computes target eligibility from Shift (GetAsyncKeyState(16)); for character-target/all skills it flips that Shift interpretation only when IsGoodSkillForActor is true. Ally party/guild can suppress attack eligibility, while PK-state/PK-zone/event-PvP and siege rules alter that suppression; m_isNoShift==1 forces the subsequent eligibility variable true. The live PC must be in a non-dead state (stateId != 3) for the normal active-target branch. ProcessPcPick repeats equivalent group/PK/Shift gates. At click BTN_DOWN, an eligible PC plus no Alt enters the approach/attack branch; control/siege/noCtrl gates choose path. With a pending nonzero skill-use type 2 or 4, it sends player message 41(target gid, skill id, attack range) plus 90(level); skillId==10000 bypasses overweight rejection.

click_clear_context.finding: ProcessInput picks the actor and runs ground handling before issuing mode message 78 on left BTN_DOWN. Root's trace confirms the mode78 receiver clears pending intent. Therefore background clicks with SUT_TO_CHARACTER avoid ground movement and then clear intent in the later mode78 dispatch; actor clicks are subject to their actor-specific branches before that dispatch. New skill message 0x4F replaces skill fields but does not itself chase-clear prior player proceed state.
